prerequisites: It is recommended to have acquired the basic competences of the Mathematics subject of the Degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the most common cryptographic constructions and recognize their presence in real-life digital applications.
Manipulate encryption systems, both public and private key, as well as digital signature schemes.
Skillfully handle the algebraic structures and tools involved in the different cryptographic solutions to the security problem.
Use numerical calculation techniques to analyze and solve differential equation problems in one dimension.
Calculate the discrete Fourier transform using computer programs and apply it to transformations related to signal processing.

syllabus_topics: Numerical resolution of differential problems in one dimension.
Numerical algorithms for the calculation of the discrete Fourier transform.
Alternative models to Fourier Analysis. Applications to real problems.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices / field / computer lab / language lab

assessment_methods.method: Participation in laboratory practices and presentation of assignments
Resolution of proposed exercises and tasks

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call is calculated as NF = 0.25 NTR + 0.1 NPL + 0.15 NPT + 0.25 NEX, where NTR is the grade for assignments, NPL for lab participation, NPT for exercises and tasks, and NEX for theoretical-practical exams. All grades are out of 10 points. The course is passed when NF >= 5. For students with officially recognized differentiated evaluation, and in extraordinary calls, NF = 0.4 NTR + 0.6 NEX, where NTR is the grade for two assignments and NEX for a final objective theoretical-practical long-answer test. The course is passed when NF >= 5.
